subject: Dedicated GPU queueing window negotiation - time-sliced carveout request
messages:

To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@oriontech.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU carveout for nightly batch window / throughput ask

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we scope the Dedicated pool for OrionTech (deal RDW-2026-4892) our infra team surfaced a recurring issue: our nightly batch jobs (00:00-04:00 local) need deterministic throughput for model scoring that currently contends with customer-facing traffic. In practice we need a soft carveout so those jobs see consistent concurrency and have reduced preemption risk.

Can Redwood offer a time-sliced queueing carveout — e.g., guaranteed token throughput for a 4-hr window each night with a lower preemption weight — and if so, how would that affect our reserved GPU commit and pricing?

Attached is a simple production window export to illustrate job timing. Happy to jump on a quick call.

Attachments: [orion_production_windows.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Thanks,
Liam O'Sullivan
Head of Infrastructure
OrionTech
liam@oriontech.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Sullivan <liam@oriontech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU carveout for nightly batch window / throughput ask

Liam —

Appreciate the detail and the spreadsheet. We can support a time-sliced carveout pattern; there are a few ways to implement it depending on the tolerance for cost and preemption guarantees:

- Option A: Reserved carveout window (hard reservation) — guarantees X tokens/sec during 00:00-04:00; requires an increase in reserved commit (or conversion of burst credits into a nightly allocation).
- Option B: Priority queueing token (soft carveout) — maintains your existing commit but gives batch jobs higher queue priority and reduced preemption probability; no change to monthly commit but subject to limited headroom.
- Option C: Hybrid — small reserved buffer + priority tokens to handle spikes.

I'll loop David for a technical feasibility note and Marissa to flag commercial impacts.

Propose a 30-min sync tomorrow to align on the traffic profile and a pricing delta.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
[evelyn_hart@redwood.ai]

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU carveout for nightly batch window / throughput ask

Eve / Marissa —

Quick technical read: the carveout is doable with minimal changes to the runtime. A few things I need from Orion to precisely size the buffer:

1) typical token/sec during the batch window (avg and 95th)
2) number of concurrent batch jobs and per-job sequence length distribution
3) acceptable latency ceiling (p50/p95) for batch jobs during the window

Implementation options:
- Time-sliced reservation: create an allocation that is active 00:00-04:00 on the dedicated pool. We can enforce a deterministic throughput floor by reserving queue tokens and mapping them to GPUS; this reduces preemption to near-zero but will tie up capacity.
- Priority token queueing: use weighted scheduling and KV cache affinity to favor batch jobs — much lower cost but not a hard SLA (we can bake an SLO with credits).

I'll attach a rough sizing template so Orion can fill in numbers; happy to run the numbers once we have the CSV.

Attachments: [queue_sizing_estimate.csv]

—David
David Kim
Principal Infrastructure Engineer — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Sullivan <liam@oriontech.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU carveout for nightly batch window / throughput ask

Liam —

Couple quick commercial notes from our side:
- If Orion chooses the hard reservation (Option A) we need to adjust the reserved commit in the contract; that typically moves to an annualized SKU uplift (we can show the delta).
- For the soft priority tokens (Option B) we can include a service-level credit mechanism tied to a defined SLO (e.g., token throughput floor and preemption rate). This is faster to enable and keeps committed spend unchanged.
- Hybrid (Option C) usually lands best for customers who want predictability but little capex uplift — small nightly reserve + priority fallback.

From a sales timeline perspective, if procurement wants contractual language, please have your legal share wording for carveout duration (start/end dates, recurrence) and we can draft an SLA addendum.

Looping Ben for finance scoring on the pricing delta.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Sullivan <liam@oriontech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora.patel@oriontech.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@oriontech.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU carveout for nightly batch window / throughput ask

Evelyn / Marissa —

Thanks — attached is the filled production windows sheet and a short note from our legal/procurement on desired carveout language. Key numbers: average batch concurrency 18 jobs, typical per-job sequence length 1.2k tokens, target p95 latency under 800ms during the window. We prefer the hybrid approach but would accept Option B with an SLO backed credit mechanism if a hard reservation materially increases cost.

Attached: orion_production_windows_filled.xlsx, orion_sla_template.docx

We can do the sync Thursday morning if that works for your team.

Cheers,
Liam

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood draft: nightly carveout SLO addendum (v1)

Liam —

Thanks for the details and the template. Attached is a first-pass SLO addendum that maps the hybrid option into contract language: a nightly reserved buffer (2 GPUs equivalent / 00:00-04:00 local) plus priority token scheduling for overflow, with a simple credit mechanism if measured throughput falls below the floor more than 3 nights in a 30-day window.

High level next steps:
1) Review the attached draft (rdw_sla_draft_v1.pdf) and the queueing diagram.
2) If the wording looks good, we prepare a contractual addendum and an implementation runbook (we propose a 30-day canary).
3) Marissa will raise the pricing amendment; Ben is available for the finance review call.

If you'd like I can push a version that uses an hourly token floor instead of a GPU count — David included the sizing template that will make that mapping precise.

Attachments: [rdw_sla_draft_v1.pdf (PDF), queueing-diagram.png (image)]

Best,
Evelyn Hart
